newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Alliance volatility trades dominate.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Alliance volatility trades dominate.

text.p: Interest in newly-quoted Alliance & Leicester shares spilled over into the London equities options market, after the bank's shares got off to a much better than expected start on Monday, fuelled by bid speculation and hopes of a possible buy-back.
The shares rocketed to 571.5p in early afternoon trade, compared with an estimated trading range of 385-435p made by the bank's advisers last October.
The main options deal of the day involved the purchase of 250 July 600 calls and 550 puts at a combined cost of 42p in a strangle trade.
Dealers said the investor was betting on volatility and the strategy will make a profit if the underlying share price moves well above 600p or below 550p at the time of expiration.
The investor will suffer a maximum loss of 42p plus commissions, if Alliance and Leicester shares are trading anywhere between 550p and 600p at the time of expiration.

"We've seen quite a few reasonable size trades in Alliance & Leicester today, some good two way business in calls and puts," said one trader. "The stock has had quite a rise today, people that have failed to get hold of stock are selling puts and people wanting exposure to the stock are buying calls."
Dealers also noted interest in Marks & Spencers but elsewhere trade was extremely quiet. This was reflected in the cash market, where volume totalled 421 million by 1405 GMT.
A call spread was executed in Marks & Spencer, in which July 460 calls were bought and July 500 calls and 200 July 460 puts were sold.
The net cost of the spread was 26-1/2p, dealers said.
"That call spread is worth between 0-40p," a trader said. "The closer the underlying share price gets to 460 it's worth nothing and the closer to 500 its worth 40p."
Shares in retailer Marks & Spencer were up 5p at 499-1/2p by 1441 GMT.
